files.performance_notes: DUM on beat 1 and beat 7 of the 12-beat cycle; light tek ornaments at beat 5. Al-Ṭawīl's long half-verse aligns with the 12-unit span; maintain stately, unhurried tempo.
DUM on beat 1; tek fills on beats 3 and 5. The 8-beat Wahda Kabira cycle pairs with Al-Ṭawīl's half-verse moras; keep tempo restrained to honor the meter's epic weight.
DUM on beats 1 and 5; ka strokes on 3 and 7 provide subtle lift. Masmudi Kabir's steady 8-beat pulse supports Al-Ṭawīl's measured cadence; avoid ornamentation that disrupts the verse's epic sweep.
DUM anchors the opening of each foot-group across the 32-unit span; minimal fills preserve classical gravitas. Al-Ṭawīl's full verse maps onto the extended Warshan cycle with regal austerity.
DUM on beat 1; light tek on beat 2, ka on beat 3. Each مُتَفَاعِلُنْ foot aligns with one 3/4 bar; ornamental fills at the cycle's end accelerate toward the qaflah.
DUM on beat 1; tek on beat 4, ka ornaments on 3 and 6. One Yuruk Semai bar equals two مُتَفَاعِلُنْ feet; the lively compound feel energizes Al-Kāmil's lyrical flow.
DUM on beats 1 and 4; tek-ka fill on beat 3. Sudasi's 6-beat frame holds two مُتَفَاعِلُنْ feet; maintain moderate tempo to let Al-Kāmil's folk-lyrical quality breathe.
DUM on beats 1 and 3; tek on 2 and 4. Al-Basīṭ's binary stress of مستفعلن aligns squarely with Maqsum's DUM-tek grid; keep tempo firm and even to project oratorical clarity.

DUM on beat 1; tek-ka ornaments in the second half of the bar. Wahda's single strong DUM reinforces Al-Basīṭ's opening long syllable; tempo should feel deliberate, allowing the verse's weight to resonate.
DUM on beat 1; tek on beat 4; ka on beat 5. Nawakht's 4+3 division echoes مستفعلن+فاعلن; Al-Basīṭ's binary structure settles naturally but requires careful metric alignment in performance.
DUM-DUM-tek-DUM pattern of Sa'idi gives Al-Basīṭ a folk-oratorical drive; the opening double-DUM lands on the long syllable of مستفعلن, amplifying its declamatory force.
DUM on beat 1 of each 3/4 bar; the swaying مُفَاعَلَتُنْ foot mirrors Sama'i Darij's compound pulse. Light ornamental fills on beat 3 enhance Al-Wāfir's emotional sway.
DUM on beat 1; tek on beat 4; ka fills on 3 and 6. Yuruk Semai's lively compound pulse imparts momentum to Al-Wāfir's emotional sway; performers accelerate through the short foot-ending.
DUM on the downbeat of each 3/8 bar; light tek on beat 2, ka ornament on beat 3. The faster ternary pulse of Sama'i Saraband brings out Al-Wāfir's swaying emotional quality.
DUM on beat 1; soft tek-ka fills on beats 2 and 3. Wahda's flowing single-DUM cycle suits Al-Ramal's gentle غزل character; tempo should feel like a languid, unhurried sway.
DUM on 1 and 3; light tek on 2 and 4. Maqsum drives Al-Ramal at a brisker tarab pace; subtle ka ornaments on the second beat soften the pulse to suit the meter's delicacy.
DUM on bar 1 of the 7-bar Sama'i Darij cycle; gentle tek-ka fills highlight فَاعِلَاتُنْ's swing. Al-Ramal's supple character surfaces naturally in muwashshah and qudud settings.
DUM on beat 1; tek on beat 3; second DUM on beat 7 of the 10-beat cycle. Al-Ramal's muwashshah settings traditionally use Sama'i Thaqil; tempo is deliberate and stately.
DUM on beats 1 and 3; tek on 2 and 4. Maqsum's symmetrical DUM-tek pairs map cleanly onto مُسْتَفْعِلُنْ's even stress; keep steady tempo to support Al-Rajaz's didactic narrative flow.
DUM on beat 1; tek-ka fills on beats 2–3; gentle resolution on beat 4. Wahda's measured single-DUM cycle gives Al-Rajaz's narrative verse a calm, recitative quality.
DUM-DUM-tek-tek-DUM of Baladi lends Al-Rajaz a warm folk flavor; the first DUM aligns with مستفعلن's opening stress. Moderate fills; avoid heavy ornamentation that disrupts narrative clarity.
DUM on beat 1 and beat 7; tek ornaments at beat 4. The 12-unit Mudawwar Masri cycle accommodates a full Al-Rajaz half-verse; maintain deliberate pace to serve the didactic text.
DUM on beat 1; tek on beat 3; second DUM on beat 7. The 10-beat Sama'i Thaqil maps onto فاعلاتن مستفعلن فاعلاتن's mixed syllabic units; a canonical muwashshah pairing since the 10th century.
DUM on beat 1; tek-ka at beats 4 and 7. Jurjina's slow 10-beat cycle provides expressive space for Al-Khafīf's mixed foot; ornamental ziyāda are applied sparingly between syllable groups.
DUM on beat 1; tek on beat 5; ka fills on beats 3 and 8. Mudawwar Shami's 10-beat Levantine cycle frames Al-Khafīf elegantly in Syrian muwashshah; sustain legato between strokes.
DUM on beats 1 and 5; tek on 3 and 7. The 8-beat Masmudi Kabir requires textual adaptation to fit Al-Khafīf's 10-unit mixed foot; suitable for popular folk-style vocal settings.
DUM on beats 1 and 5; tek on 3 and 7. Eight units accommodate four فَعُولُنْ feet per half-verse; Al-Mutaqārib's epic character is amplified by Masmudi Kabir's stately cadence.
Single DUM on beat 1; tek-ka fills at beat 5. Wahda Kabira's slow 8-beat cycle gives Al-Mutaqārib's heroic verse a grand processional feel; avoid rushed ornamental fills.
DUM on beat 1; syncopated tek on beat 3-and; ka ornaments throughout. Ciftetelli's Ottoman-Arab flavor lends Al-Mutaqārib an exotic epic color; maintain sensuous legato between strokes.
DUM on 1 and 3; tek on 2 and 4. Maqsum's faster 4-beat frame suits Al-Mutaqārib in nashīd and patriotic settings; tek fills on offbeats sharpen the heroic forward drive.
DUM on beat 1; tek-ka on the second eighth note; rapid ziyāda fills between DUM strokes heighten Al-Hazaj's festive energy. Drive tempo upward during vocal refrains.
DUM-tek-tek-DUM pattern pairs naturally with مَفَاعِيلُنْ's long syllable; light ka ornaments on offbeats. Moderate tempo suits Al-Hazaj's cheerful folk character without losing rhythmic clarity.
DUM on beat 1; tek-ka fills on the second half of the bar. Wahda Saghira moderates Al-Hazaj's festive pace; light ornamental rolls sustain forward motion through مَفَاعِيلُنْ's extended syllable.
DUM on the downbeat; rapid tek-tek-ka fills on the second beat drive Al-Sarī's energetic forward motion. Ziyāda ornaments between DUM strokes match the meter's brisk syllabic pace.
DUM-tek-DUM-tek of Fallahi maps onto مستفعلن مستفعلن; the double DUM reinforces Al-Sarī's driving energy. Folk ornamental fills suit open-air ensemble performance contexts.
DUM-tek-tek-DUM of Ayyub provides syncopated contrast to Al-Sarī's even stress; use light ka ornaments on the second eighth note to maintain the meter's energetic momentum.
DUM on beat 1; tek-ka ornaments on the second half. Wahda Saghira at moderate tempo suits more controlled renditions of Al-Sarī; pace remains vivacious while allowing textual intelligibility.
DUM on 1 and 3; tek on 2 and 4. Maqsum's binary pulse cleanly accommodates فَاعِلُنْ's stress pairs; this is the most idiomatic pairing for contemporary Al-Mutadārak settings.

DUM on the downbeat; rapid tek-ka ornaments fill the second beat. Malfuf's breakneck pace showcases Al-Mutadārak's fluid syllabic chain; ziyāda rolls between DUM strokes amplify the meter's modern energy.
DUM-tek-DUM-tek of Fallahi drives Al-Mutadārak at a folk pace; the even DUM placement aligns with فَاعِلُنْ's stress. Light riq fills add a rural Egyptian texture to the verse.
DUM on beat 1; tek-ka ornaments at beats 2–3; gentle resolution on beat 4. Wahda's measured cycle suits calmer Al-Mutadārak settings; space between strokes allows melodic phrasing to resonate.
DUM on beat 1; tek on beat 4; ka on beat 5. Nawakht's 4+3 division maps precisely onto فَاعِلَاتُنْ+فَاعِلُنْ; Al-Madīd's elegiac tone is served by restrained ornaments and measured pace.
DUM on beat 1; tek on beat 4; light ka on beat 6. Dawr Hindi's lighter 7/8 feel gives Al-Madīd's elegiac verse a floating quality; ornamental fills are used sparingly throughout.
DUM on beat 1 of each 3/4 bar; soft tek ornaments on beat 2. Sama'i Darij requires textual adjustment to fit Al-Madīd's 4+3 foot; used only in Andalusian qudud contexts.
